result: Myeloid-specific deletion of miR-17~92 family miRNAs causes obesity in mice under both regular chow and high-fat diet conditions, as demonstrated by increased body weight, visceral adipose tissue (VAT) weight, and total adipose tissue measured by MRI. Bone marrow chimera experiments confirm this is a myeloid cell-intrinsic effect.
evaluation: Claims C3, C8-C17 collectively demonstrate obesity phenotypes in TKO mice through multiple independent measurements (body weight, VAT weight, MRI quantification) under different dietary conditions (regular chow and HFD), with bone marrow chimera experiments (C15-C17) establishing cell-intrinsic causality. The data are consistent across multiple experimental approaches and include appropriate controls.

result: Myeloid-specific deletion of miR-17~92 family miRNAs results in compromised glucose tolerance in mice.
evaluation: Claims C4 and C18 are supported by glucose tolerance test data shown in Figure 2A. The GTT demonstrates impaired glucose clearance in TKO mice compared to controls, with statistical significance indicated. This metabolic phenotype is consistent with the obesity observed in these mice.

result: Deletion of miR-17~92 family miRNAs shifts adipose tissue macrophages (ATMs) toward a spontaneous inflammatory phenotype characterized by increased TNF and decreased IL-10 expression, without altering ATM population size. This inflammatory shift is supported by RNA-seq analysis showing enrichment of inflammatory response genes.
evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C20-C22, C24-C29 are well-supported by multiple lines of evidence including serum cytokine measurements (C20), tissue qPCR (C21-C22), flow cytometry showing unchanged ATM populations (C24-C25), RNA-seq with GO analysis (C26-C27), and direct ATM gene expression analysis (C28). The data consistently demonstrate an inflammatory phenotype in TKO ATMs.

result: In bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs), miR-17~92 family miRNAs suppress TNF-mediated inflammation by promoting IL-10 expression. IL-10 supplementation rescues TNF overproduction in TKO cells, and anti-TNF treatment reverses obesity in TKO mice, establishing TNF as a functional downstream target.
evaluation: Claims C30-C39 are supported by comprehensive in vitro experiments showing altered cytokine expression at mRNA (C30-C32) and protein levels (C33), IL-10 supplementation rescue experiments (C34), IL-10R blockade experiments (C35), and critically, in vivo anti-TNF treatment that reverses obesity (C37). The mechanistic link between IL-10 deficiency and TNF overproduction is well-established through these experiments.

result: The three miRNA clusters of the miR-17~92 family function collectively to regulate TNF and IL-10 expression in macrophages. TNF upregulation requires deletion of all three clusters, while IL-10 downregulation correlates with the number of deleted clusters.
evaluation: Claims C40-C44 are supported by systematic analysis of single, double, and triple knockout macrophages shown in Figure 4. The data demonstrate functional redundancy among the three clusters for TNF regulation (C40, C42) and a dose-dependent effect on IL-10 expression (C41, C43), establishing the collective nature of their regulatory function.

result: miR-17~92 family miRNAs promote IL-10 production by sustaining expression of the transcription factor Fos, a key component of AP-1 that drives IL-10 transcription. Fos is specifically downregulated in TKO macrophages at both mRNA and protein levels, and Fos overexpression rescues IL-10 expression and suppresses TNF in TKO cells.
evaluation: Claims C5, C49-C56 are well-supported by RNA-seq data identifying Fos downregulation (C50), qPCR and immunoblotting confirmation (C52), specificity demonstrated by unchanged Jun expression (C53), and functional rescue experiments with Fos overexpression (C54). The mechanistic link between Fos and IL-10 is supported by prior literature (C49) and validated experimentally.

result: miR-17~92 family miRNAs directly target the transcription factor YY1 to promote Fos expression. YY1 protein (but not mRNA) is increased in TKO macrophages, YY1 is a predicted and validated direct target of miR-17 family miRNAs by luciferase assays, and YY1 knockdown increases Fos expression and restores IL-10/TNF balance.
evaluation: Claims C6, C7, C57-C67 establish a complete regulatory pathway with multiple lines of evidence: post-transcriptional regulation of YY1 (C58-C60), bioinformatic prediction (C61), direct targeting validated by luciferase assays with wild-type and mutant constructs (C62-C64), and functional validation through YY1 knockdown experiments (C65-C66). The pathway is supported by prior literature on YY1-Fos interaction (C57).

result: The regulation of TNF and IL-10 by miR-17~92 family miRNAs is independent of PTEN, despite PTEN being a well-established target of these miRNAs.
evaluation: Claims C47-C48 are supported by chemical inhibitor experiments showing that PTEN inhibition does not alter IL-10 or TNF expression in TKO macrophages (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B). This negative result is important for establishing the specificity of the YY1-Fos pathway and ruling out a major known target of these miRNAs.

result: The miR-17~92 family consists of three paralogous clusters encoding 13 distinct mature miRNAs that can be divided into four subfamilies based on seed regions.
evaluation: Claims C78-C79 describe the structural organization of the miRNA family, supported by schematic diagrams (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B) and citations to established literature. This is well-established background information accurately presented.

result: Prior work has established that global miR-17~92 deletion causes embryonic lethality while individual cluster deletions have minimal phenotypes, and these miRNAs function in development, tumorigenesis, and lymphocyte biology, but their role in myeloid cells remains poorly understood.
evaluation: Claims C68-C72 accurately summarize prior literature with appropriate citations (Ventura et al., 2008; Mendell, 2008; Mogilyansky and Rigoutsos, 2013; Kang et al., 2013; Lai et al., 2016; Xiao et al., 2008). This provides appropriate context for the current study's focus on myeloid cells.

result: TNF and IL-10 are critical regulators of insulin sensitivity and obesity, macrophages are the major source of these cytokines in adipose tissue, and disruption of the balance between pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines is linked to inflammatory and metabolic diseases.
evaluation: Claims C19, C23, C73-C77 accurately summarize established knowledge from the literature with appropriate citations (Chawla et al., 2011; Olefsky and Glass, 2010; Mosser and Edwards, 2008; Sugimoto et al., 2019; Bain and Mowat, 2014; Odegaard and Chawla, 2011). This provides essential background for understanding the significance of the findings.

result: MicroRNAs are short non-coding RNAs that regulate gene expression post-transcriptionally through a well-characterized biogenesis pathway, and approximately 25-40% are organized in clusters that may function coordinately.
evaluation: Claims C80-C83 accurately describe established microRNA biology with appropriate citations (Krol et al., 2010; Altuvia et al., 2005; Kozomara and Griffiths-Jones, 2014). This provides necessary background information for readers unfamiliar with microRNA biology.

result: Prior work has established multiple targets of miR-17~92 family miRNAs (including PTEN, E2F1, Bim, PHLPP2, C/EBPβ) and mechanisms by which TNF promotes insulin resistance and IL-10 suppresses inflammation through specific transcription factors.
evaluation: Claims C45-C46, C84-C88 accurately summarize relevant prior literature with appropriate citations. This provides important context for the mechanistic studies and helps position the identification of YY1 as a novel target within the broader understanding of these miRNAs.

result: miR-17~92 family miRNAs are key positive regulators of IL-10 production in adipose tissue macrophages and represent potential therapeutic targets for inflammatory and metabolic disorders.
evaluation: Claim C89 is supported by the experimental data presented. However, claim C90 regarding therapeutic potential is speculative and not directly tested. While the functional importance is established, translation to therapeutic applications would require additional validation including assessment of specificity, delivery methods, and efficacy in disease models beyond the genetic knockout approach used here.
